# Confirm PQC base image variant availability and RHEL 9.8 rebase date with AIPCC

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's two dependency unknowns with the AIPCC team, both tracked under the RHOAIENG-7195 spike:

1. Whether PQC variants of the `ubi9/python-311`, `ubi9/python-312`, `ubi9/python-312-minimal`, and `ubi9/nodejs-22` base images will be available for RHOAI 3.6, and their committed delivery dates. These variants are currently unconfirmed; roughly eleven RHOAI images (training variants, lmes-job, feature-server, dashboard) build on them and have no confirmed PQC target base.
2. The committed date of the AIPCC RHEL 9.8 rebase (AIPCC-7258), which gates adoption of the `rhel9-8-els/pqc-minimal` base image by the ~34 RHOAI images currently built on `rhel9-6-els/rhel:9.6-*` bases.

Both questions are attributed to the same AIPCC coordination effort and produce one deliverable, so they are combined into a single investigation. The answers determine whether the affected image families proceed with base image switches or fall back to OCP exception filings, and they populate the target-base entries of the PQC readiness matrix.

## Scope

- Engage with the AIPCC team (via the RHOAIENG-7195 spike and AIPCC-7258) to obtain, per base image (python-311, python-312, python-312-minimal, nodejs-22): a confirmed availability status and a committed delivery date.
- Obtain the committed date for the AIPCC RHEL 9.8 rebase that gates `rhel9-8-els/pqc-minimal` adoption.
- Verify claimed-available images in registry.redhat.io (e.g., that published PQC variants report `DEFAULT:PQ` under `update-crypto-policies --show`), consistent with the August 2026 confirmation for `ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc` and `rhel9-8-els/pqc-minimal`.
- Record the outcome per image family: switch-by-deadline confirmed, or not-available-in-time (triggering OCP exception filings by the affected component teams).
- Escalate per the strategy's risk mitigation if no committed date is obtained by early September.
- Communicate outcomes to the component teams whose images depend on each answer, and to the PQC readiness matrix. Sequencing: the matrix is maintained by the compliance coordination work stream, which stands it up as its first deliverable with unresolved fields (including the python/nodejs target bases) authored as TBD — matrix creation therefore precedes the first outcome publication, and this investigation's outcomes land as in-place updates to existing entries rather than queueing behind matrix creation.

Out of scope: building or delivering the base image variants themselves (AIPCC's deliverable, tracked in their own pipeline); filing OCP exceptions (each component team files its own); Go ML-KEM, TLSAdherence, and TLS-scanner CI (owned by RHAISTRAT-7816).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of `ubi9/python-311`, `ubi9/python-312`, `ubi9/python-312-minimal`, and `ubi9/nodejs-22` has a recorded availability status and committed delivery date, sourced from the AIPCC team.
- The AIPCC RHEL 9.8 rebase (AIPCC-7258) has a recorded committed date, with an explicit statement of whether it lands before the September 15, 2026 deadline.
- Any image verified as available in registry.redhat.io is checked to report `DEFAULT:PQ` crypto policy, with the check command and output recorded.
- A per-family go/no-go determination is published to the component teams whose images depend on each answer and recorded in the PQC readiness matrix (against entries already stood up by the compliance coordination work stream — the determination resolves those entries' TBD target bases in place): which image families can complete the PQC base switch for RHOAI 3.6 and which must fall back to OCP exception filings.
- If any committed date is missing as of early September, an escalation is raised per the strategy's risk mitigation (escalate if no committed date by early September).

## HLR Traceability

- **[P0] All RHOAI runtime images must use a PQC-enabled base image for RHOAI 3.6 / OCP 5.0** — this investigation unblocks (or redirects to exceptions) the python/nodejs-based and rhel9-ELS-based image families, which together account for ~45 of the payload's images.
- Supports the Dependencies table entries: PQC variants of python-311/312/nodejs (unconfirmed) and AIPCC RHEL 9.8 rebase (gates RHEL9-ELS image adoption).

## Risks and Assumptions Carried Forward

- Risk: PQC variants of python-311/312/nodejs not available in time — teams using those bases may need OCP exceptions (mitigated by this investigation and early-September escalation).
- Risk: AIPCC RHEL 9.8 rebase slips — teams using rhel9-6-els may need exceptions.
- Assumption: `ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc` and `rhel9-8-els/pqc-minimal` are available and activate DEFAULT:PQ policy (confirmed August 2026, OCPSTRAT-7413) — not re-litigated here.

# Switch ubi9-minimal-based runtime images to ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc

## Description

This epic coordinates the PQC base image switch campaign for the ~68 RHOAI runtime images currently built on `ubi9/ubi-minimal:latest` — Go operators and most platform components — switching each image's final runtime stage to `registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc` (confirmed available, reports `DEFAULT:PQ`). The target base is confirmed available, so this campaign starts immediately with no dependency on the AIPCC confirmation work.

Per the strategy, each image's owning component team executes the final-stage base swap in its own repository via its tracking ticket linked to the parent strategy; this epic coordinates the campaign: build pipeline updates, per-team tracking, and verification that every image in the family is switched (or covered by an OCP exception).

## Scope

- Campaign coordination across the component teams owning ubi9-minimal-based images (Go operators and most platform components), using the RHOAI 3.5 CSV relatedImages list (153 relatedImages) and the locally maintained organized image inventory to enumerate the ~68 images in this family.
- Coordinate build pipeline updates so builds reference `ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc` (e.g., RHOAI-Build-Config references and per-repo pipeline configuration).
- Track each image's switch via the owning team's tracking ticket linked to the parent strategy; chase unlinked tickets weekly per the strategy's mitigation for missed deadlines.
- Only the final runtime stage of each Dockerfile/Containerfile changes — no builder image change (PQC enablement is runtime only).
- Note for Go components: ML-KEM arrives via native Go crypto regardless of base; the switch is for platform consistency (confirmed assumption, July 2026). The switch must not change HA characteristics (no replica or availability changes).
- Includes images of components whose TLS stack is not OpenSSL-backed (e.g., the Rust guardrails orchestrator, whose TLS remediation is tracked separately): the base switch here delivers platform consistency and system-OpenSSL compliance, while those components' ML-KEM negotiation capability is resolved by their own remediation work or OCP exceptions.

Out of scope: OCP exception filing (each team files its own via OCPEXCEPT); Go ML-KEM, TLSAdherence, TLS-scanner CI (RHAISTRAT-7816); post-OCP-5.0 base image evolution (micro images, Hummingbird/UBI10); FIPS+PQC combined support (incompatible on UBI9).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every image in the ubi9-minimal family has its final runtime stage rebuilt on `ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc`, or is covered by a filed and acknowledged OCP exception with a documented remediation plan — zero unaccounted-for images remain in this family.
- For each switched image, `update-crypto-policies --show` executed inside the container reports `DEFAULT:PQ`, and `openssl list -kem-algorithms` reports ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024, verified by the automated payload CI scan.
- No Dockerfile/Containerfile builder stage changed in any switched image; only the final runtime stage base reference changed.
- Build pipelines for all switched images reference `ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc` and produce green builds.
- No replica count, availability, or HA characteristic changed as a result of the switch.
- Rollback: each base swap is revertible by restoring the prior base image reference in the component repository and rebuilding (documented per tracking ticket).
- All family tracking tickets are linked to the parent strategy for the aggregated OCP 5.0 compliance view.

## HLR Traceability

- **[P0] All RHOAI runtime images must use a PQC-enabled base image (`ubi9-minimal-pqc`, `rhel9-8-els/pqc-minimal`, or equivalent) for RHOAI 3.6 / OCP 5.0** — delivers the switch for the largest family (~68 images).
- **[P0] PQC enablement is runtime only — only the final stage of the Dockerfile/Containerfile changes; no builder image change needed** — encoded as a scope constraint and acceptance criterion.
- Supports strategy AC-1 (per-family pass criteria) and AC-2 (switched-or-exceptioned accounting).

## Assumptions Carried Forward

- Go components get ML-KEM via native Go crypto; the base switch is for platform consistency (confirmed July 2026).
- PQC hybrid key exchange is negotiated opportunistically — clients without PQC support continue via classic ECDHE (backwards compatibility preserved by the base image's OpenSSL).
- Strategy-level Licence Validation gate is pending human review; a base image content swap is not expected to change transitive dependency licensing, but the gate must clear before ship.

## Description

A base image swap cannot remediate this component: rustls+ring does not use system OpenSSL, so it inherits nothing from a PQC-enabled base image. The spike's outcome determines the migration approach and effort for the remediation work that follows, and informs whether the team can meet the September 15 deadline through migration or must file an OCP exception.

## Scope

- Determine viable migration paths for the orchestrator's TLS stack to negotiate ML-KEM hybrid key exchange (e.g., X25519MLKEM768), evaluating options against the current rustls+ring dependency set (rustls, hyper-rustls, tokio-rustls, tonic TLS features as recorded in the component's architecture context).
- Assess each path's compatibility with the service's TLS surfaces: optional inbound TLS/mTLS on the API server, per-service downstream TLS configuration (detector, chunker, generation clients), and the optional X-Forwarded-Access-Token rewrite behavior.
- Produce an effort estimate and feasibility assessment for landing the migration before the September 15, 2026 deadline.
- Verify backwards compatibility requirements: PQC hybrid key exchange is negotiated opportunistically — non-PQC TLS 1.3 clients must continue working via classic ECDHE.
- Record the recommended path and the fallback determination (migrate vs. file an OCP exception documenting the TLS stack and remediation plan).

Out of scope: executing the migration (follow-on remediation work); the orchestrator's ubi9-minimal base image switch (part of the platform-wide switch campaign, which delivers platform consistency but not ML-KEM for this component); Go ML-KEM and TLSAdherence (RHAISTRAT-7816); ML-DSA certificates (deferred).

- Each path is assessed for effect on the service's optional TLS/mTLS and per-service downstream TLS configuration behavior — no reduction in existing TLS capabilities without explicit documentation.
- An effort estimate and September 15 feasibility determination is recorded for the recommended path.

# Automated payload CI scan for PQC crypto policy compliance

## Description

This epic builds the automated CI scan that measures the strategy's primary acceptance criterion: across the RHOAI 3.6 payload, every switched container reports `DEFAULT:PQ` as its active crypto policy and exposes ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024 via `openssl list -kem-algorithms`. The scan provides the per-image and payload-level compliance verification for the base image switch campaigns.

This is distinct from the TLS-scanner CI owned by RHAISTRAT-7816 (which tests TLS handshake PQC negotiation): this scan verifies container crypto policy and KEM algorithm availability inside the shipped images.

## Scope

- Build a CI job that, for each image in the RHOAI 3.6 payload (enumerated from the RHOAI-Build-Config CSV relatedImages list), executes `update-crypto-policies --show` and `openssl list -kem-algorithms` inside the container and compares against expected values (`DEFAULT:PQ`; ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, ML-KEM-1024 present).
- Produce a per-image and aggregated compliance report across the payload, consumable by the PQC readiness matrix and compliance coordination tracking.
- Encode the criterion's documented exclusions: the check applies to OpenSSL-backed components only — components using non-OpenSSL TLS stacks (rustls+ring, Java/NSS) are accounted for by OCP exception filings rather than this scan; on FIPS-mode clusters, FIPS policy deactivates PQC for this release, so `DEFAULT:PQ` non-functionality there is expected and not a compliance failure.
- Run the scan in CI on the payload build so compliance is measured continuously as images switch.

Out of scope: TLS handshake negotiation testing (TLS-scanner CI, owned by RHAISTRAT-7816); Go ML-KEM testing (RHOAIENG-7334, RHAISTRAT-7816); remediating non-compliant images (the switch campaigns' scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The scan executes across the full RHOAI 3.6 payload and produces a per-image compliance result (policy `DEFAULT:PQ`; ML-KEM-512/768/1024 present) plus an aggregated report.
- OpenSSL-backed images that have completed the base image switch pass the scan; failures identify the image and failing check.
- Components using non-OpenSSL TLS stacks are excluded from pass/fail and cross-referenced against the exception-tracking accounting instead.
- FIPS-mode clusters are handled per the documented exclusion: PQC deactivation under FIPS policy for this release is reported as expected behavior, not a compliance failure.
- The scan runs as part of CI on the payload (not only as a one-off), so the final RHOAI 3.6 payload measurement is reproducible.

## HLR Traceability

- **[P0] All RHOAI runtime images must use a PQC-enabled base image... for RHOAI 3.6 / OCP 5.0** — this epic is the "measured by automated CI scan across the RHOAI 3.6 payload" clause of strategy AC-1.
- **[P0] Teams unable to comply by September 15 must file an OCP exception...** — the scan's exclusion accounting cross-references exception-covered components, supporting the zero-unaccounted-images outcome of AC-2.

## Assumptions Carried Forward

- The image list for RHOAI 3.6 follows the RHOAI-Build-Config CSV relatedImages pattern (153 relatedImages for 3.5) and the locally maintained organized inventory; the scan enumerates from the 3.6 equivalent.
- X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange is backwards-compatible with non-PQC TLS 1.3 clients (IETF hybrid key exchange draft) — the scan checks algorithm availability, not client compatibility.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-8001 (Base image compliance — Post-quantum cryptography support)

## Triage Decision

Full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only). The strategy is S-sized, but it affects all RHOAI component images (~153 relatedImages across every component team), names three distinct impacted teams, and contains genuine unknowns whose answers change which downstream epics exist (PQC variants of python/nodejs base images, AIPCC RHEL 9.8 rebase date, Rust TLS postures). The below-threshold escape conditions for genuine unknowns and multiple architecturally distinct work streams both apply.

## Decomposition Approach

The strategy is a compliance coordination tracker: each component team owns switching its images or filing an OCP exception, and links its tracking tickets to the parent strategy for aggregated visibility. The epic set therefore follows the strategy's own decomposition axes:

- **Base-image-family switch campaigns** — one epic per row of the strategy's base image mapping table. Each campaign is a single logical change (final runtime stage swap to one named target base) executed per owning team via linked tracking tickets; the campaign epic is coordinated by the DevOps/Build team, whose stated involvement is coordinating base image pipeline updates.
- **Named component remediations** — fms-guardrails-orchestrator (rustls+ring) and trainer data cache (Rust TLS posture unknown) each get an Investigation (the strategy's named spikes) plus a gated remediation Implementation.
- **Central work streams** — AIPCC base image variant confirmation (Investigation), compliance coordination/readiness matrix, automated payload CI verification scan, and performance validation.

**Component mapping notes (non-obvious mappings per Step 2):** the canonical RHAI component list has no entry for a platform-wide image campaign, so each family campaign maps to the closest parent-level canonical component: ubi9-minimal family → `AI Core Platform`; rhel9-6-els family (notebooks, workbenches, training runtimes, mlserver) → `Notebooks Images` (family also spans `Model Runtimes` and `Workbenches/IDE` images, recorded in epic scope); python/nodejs family (training variants, lmes-job, feature-server, dashboard) → `Model Runtimes` (family also spans `Feature Store` and `AI Core Dashboard` images, recorded in epic scope). fms-guardrails-orchestrator → `AI Guardrails`; trainer data cache → `Training Kubeflow` (trainer component); AIPCC base image work → `AIPCC Productization`; coordination → `DevOps`; CI scan → `CI/CD`; performance validation → `PerfScale`.
